subject: Intro + demo: BrightCart use case & volume details
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightcart.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@brightcart.com
Date: 2026-07-18T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Interest in Redwood — quick demo?

Hi Vivek,

We signed up for the self-serve sandbox last week and I kicked the tires on the embeddings + generation flows. We’re evaluating Redwood as the inference layer for BrightCart’s search and product recommendation microservice.

Primary goals: reduce search latency and cost for similarity embeddings (product-to-product), and add a lightweight generative reranking layer for queries that fall back to a more contextual response.

Quick ask: could we set up a 30–40 minute demo next week to see how Redwood would sit in our stack? I also attached a small traffic overview so you have a sense of volume.

A few immediate answers to expect on our side:
- Spike volume: peak search requests ~1200 req/s (internal edge) with 40k unique queries/minute during promos
- Monthly tokens (approx): 10–20B tokens for rerank/generation combined
- Timeline: pilot in Q4, production roll early Q1 2027

Attach: brightcart_traffic_overview.xlsx

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Platform Lead, BrightCart
platform@brightcart.com
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@brightcart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in Redwood — quick demo?

Hi Aisha — thanks for the context and the spreadsheet, that helps. I’d love to run through a short walkthrough tailored to your search + rerank flow. Before we lock time, two quick qualification items so the session is focused and we bring the right people:  

1) Critical metrics and SLOs: are you targeting p95 latency under 120ms for search, or is 200–250ms acceptable during peaks?
2) Data residency / security: will model payloads include PII or customer addresses that need to stay inside a VPC?
3) Integration: do you plan to hit Redwood via our Hosted API initially, or would you prefer Dedicated capacity right away for predictable throughput?
4) Concurrency pattern: is traffic evenly distributed or do you see short promo bursts (you mentioned promos — how long are those windows, typically 15–45m or multiple hours?)

If you can answer those, I’ll prepare a short demo that shows (a) embeddings throughput tuning, (b) generation rerank latency vs quality tradeoffs, and (c) a recommended pilot design (Hosted -> Dedicated migration path). I’ve looped Marissa (SDR) to help coordinate calendars and Ben (solutions) to bring model-sizing recommendations.

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Tue 7/21 10:00–10:40
- Tue 7/21 15:00–15:40
- Wed 7/22 09:30–10:10

Attachments: redwood_demo-deck.pdf (demo outline)

Best,

On Jul 18, 2026, at 10:02 AM, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai wrote:
> Hi Aisha — thanks for the context and the spreadsheet, that helps. I’d love to run through a short walkthrough tailored to your search + rerank flow. Before we lock time, two quick qualification items so the session is focused and we bring the right people:

> 1) Critical metrics and SLOs: are you targeting p95 latency under 120ms for search, or is 200–250ms acceptable during peaks?
> 2) Data residency / security: will model payloads include PII or customer addresses that need to stay inside a VPC?
> 3) Integration: do you plan to hit Redwood via our Hosted API initially, or would you prefer Dedicated capacity right away for predictable throughput?
> 4) Concurrency pattern: is traffic evenly distributed or do you see short promo bursts (you mentioned promos — how long are those windows, typically 15–45m or multiple hours?)

Thanks — answers below inline.

1) Latency: for core search we need p95 < 150ms during normal periods; during promos we can tolerate up to ~300ms but we need graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
2) Data: payloads will include hashed customer IDs and product SKUs — no free-form customer notes or addresses in the payloads. We need SOC2 + a standard DPA; BrightCart legal will request vendor security docs later in the process.
3) Integration: we’ll start with Hosted API to iterate fast; if the pilot shows predictable patterns we’ll look at Dedicated for Q1 roll.
4) Promos: bursts are typically 20–90 minutes, with the worst-case 2–3 hour flash windows during big seasonal events.

We can do Tue 7/21 15:00–15:40. Joining from our side: me, one engineer (Ravi), and our infra lead (Monique). Send a calendar invite and Zoom link and we’ll be there.

Thanks,
Aisha
